articles.headline: OFAC Removes Designation for Venezuela-Related Entity
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a Venezuela-related designation removal on October 14, 2026. This action indicates a change in the sanctions status for a previously designated entity or individual associated with Venezuela.

While specific details of the removed designation were not immediately released, such actions typically follow a review of the entity's activities or a shift in U.S. foreign policy objectives concerning Venezuela. This could potentially ease certain restrictions for the delisted party.
The removal comes amidst ongoing discussions regarding sanctions relief for Venezuela, particularly concerning its oil and mining sectors, which have seen temporary authorizations in the past.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. These designations aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.

The action underscores the U.S. government's continued commitment to combating international criminal enterprises and safeguarding the U.S. financial system from abuse. Designated parties face asset freezes and prohibitions on transactions with U.S. persons.
These designations are part of broader U.S. efforts to apply financial pressure on those who threaten national security through illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Reaches Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics; Issues ICC and Burma-Related Actions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026, resolving apparent violations of sanctions regulations. Concurrently, OFAC issued new designations related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and a designation removal concerning Burma.

The settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics highlights OFAC's enforcement efforts against companies failing to comply with U.S. sanctions programs. The specific details of the violations leading to the settlement were not immediately disclosed.

The ICC designations and the Burma-related removal reflect targeted adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy, addressing specific concerns related to international justice and political developments in Burma.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026. General Licenses typically authorize specific types of transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under sanctions programs.

This new General License aims to provide clarity and potentially allow for certain activities involving Russia that are deemed permissible under U.S. policy, without undermining the broader sanctions objectives.

The issuance of General Licenses can reflect adjustments to sanctions implementation, often in response to humanitarian concerns, specific industry needs, or to facilitate certain types of non-sanctionable trade.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and General License, Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and the issuance of an Iran-related General License on October 8, 2026. Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Russia-related General License.

The Iran-related designations target individuals and entities deemed to be supporting the Iranian regime's illicit activities, while the new General License may authorize specific transactions related to Iran under certain conditions.

The amendment to the Russia-related General License indicates a refinement of existing authorizations, potentially adjusting the scope of permissible activities or clarifying compliance requirements for transactions involving Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several designations removals and updates on October 5, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ).

The designations removals and updates reflect ongoing adjustments to OFAC's sanctions lists, which can occur due to various factors such as changes in circumstances, successful remediation efforts, or policy shifts.

The Iran-related Alert warns foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted without advance notice if they transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions. The amended FAQ provides further clarification on how foreign financial institutions will be informed of such findings.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Terrorism Designations on October 2, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist organizations globally.

The designations aim to disrupt the financial networks and operations of terrorist groups, preventing them from accessing the international financial system and limiting their ability to fund illicit activities.
This move reinforces the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating terrorism through financial sanctions and international cooperation.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and Updates, Transnational Criminal Organizations Designation, and New Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and designations updates on October 1, 2026. Additionally, OFAC designated a Transnational Criminal Organization and published an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ).

The Iran-related actions continue the U.S. government's pressure campaign against the Iranian regime, targeting entities involved in its proliferation activities and support for terrorism. The new Determination and amended FAQ provide further guidance on these sanctions.
The designation of a Transnational Criminal Organization underscores OFAC's broad mandate to combat illicit financial activities that threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations; Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations on September 30, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC removed designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics, and Libya.
The new designations target individuals and entities involved in terrorism and transnational criminal activities, aiming to disrupt their financial networks and operations.

The removals of designations for Belarus, counter narcotics, and Libya indicate a recalibration of sanctions policy in these areas, potentially reflecting changes in geopolitical circumstances or successful compliance efforts.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Bank of America, N.A., imposing a civil penalty of $11,662,930. This penalty addresses apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

Bank of America admitted to willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act and failing to implement and maintain an adequate anti-money laundering (AML) program. The bank processed millions of dollars in payments in apparent violation of sanctions programs due to technical and human errors, poor sanctions alert calibration, and mishandling of accounts associated with blocked persons.

The settlement amount reflects OFAC's determination that the apparent violations were non-egregious and largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. No reduction to the base penalty was granted for remedial measures or cooperation.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
